note: Travail primarily means work/labor/job. 'Workplace' is normally expressed through a construction such as au travail rather than as the bare noun's basic meaning.
Same spelling also serves as plural of fil; form-based deck includes homographs.
proposed_english: son/sons; threads/wires (plural of fil, different pronunciation/context)

note: The current gloss omits the central senses of coup and instead gives obscure/contextual ones. Learners need blow/hit, shot, stroke/move, and the many fixed-expression uses.
proposed_english: blow; hit; stroke; shot; move; sudden action/event; time/instance (in expressions)

note: Manger is primarily a verb 'to eat'. The noun label is rare/marked and is unnecessary without a noun gloss in a beginner entry.
Meilleur can mean both 'better' and 'best' depending on construction and also functions substantivally as 'the best'.
The current 'gulp down with relish' sense is slang/contextual and should not compete with the core learner meaning. Envoyer primarily means send/dispatch and can mean throw/send off.
proposed_english: to send; to dispatch; to send off; to throw (context-dependent)

note: The verbal meaning 'remember' occurs in the pronominal construction se souvenir de; the entry should make that explicit rather than presenting souvenir as an ordinary bare verb.
proposed_english: memory; souvenir; remembrance; to remember (se souvenir de)

note: The entry should label register. Merde is vulgar and is used both as a noun and an exclamation.

The POS list includes adjective and noun readings that are absent from the gloss. Pendant is 'during/for' as a preposition, while pendant also means hanging and a pendant as adjective/noun; 'while' normally appears in pendant que.
proposed_english: during; for (a duration); while (pendant que); hanging; pendant

note: Histoire centrally means both history and story; omitting 'history' is a major learner error.
Marcher centrally means walk and, very commonly, work/function ('ça marche'). 'Believe' is not a safe general gloss.
proposed_english: to walk; to work; to function; to go; to march

note: Tirer means pull/draw/shoot; 'leave a place' requires the informal pronominal construction se tirer. The gloss should distinguish it.
proposed_english: to pull; to draw; to shoot; to drag; to get away/leave (se tirer, informal)

note: Importer also very commonly means 'to matter/be important' in constructions such as peu importe / qu'importe, not only 'to import'.
proposed_english: to import; to matter; to be important (often impersonal)

note: The current gloss 'newborn' is not an appropriate core meaning. Part means part/share/portion and appears in many fixed expressions.
